deviations: Academic performance index uses the dataset's provided PCAperf variable (labelled 'Performance index 2012, PCA'); a PCA I computed on standardized GPA, exams passed and eligible-to-continue in the working sample correlates 0.995 with it but is not identical (different scaling/sample), so the provided index was preferred as the authors' construction of the paper's definition.
GPA uses the dataset's provided standardized GPA (mean -0.01, SD 1.005 in the working sample) without re-standardizing.
notes: Data: uctdata_balanced.dta (balanced panel, 499 students x 2 rounds); working sample = round-2 rows (all have both IATs at baseline and follow-up): 332 black, 117 white, 18 coloured, 32 Indian/other. Equation (2) estimated with fixest::feols, SEs clustered by baseline room (roomnum_base, unique across residences). Own controls: Female, UCT admission score (Falseuct2012), wealth index (durpcabas_nomiss), consumption (consbas_nomiss), Foreign, private school, each with the dataset's missing-value dummies (mean-imputed); roommate controls: the same except female, with their missing dummies. Table 3: follow-up Race IAT on Mixed Room + baseline Race IAT + controls + residence FE, by race. Table 4: outcomes GPA, examspassed, continue, PCAperf; subsamples with residence + academic program (regprogram) FE; full sample with White/Coloured/Indian-Other dummies and race group (black/white/other) x residence FE + program FE. Attempts 1-2 were exploratory (variable inspection, no RESULT lines). Attempt-3 printed RESULT lines but fixest's default dropped singleton fixed-effect observations (N 324/106/493 rather than the whole working sample); I set fixef.rm='none' so every working-sample student is kept, as the paper's sample definition requires. Point estimates were identical; only Ns and SEs changed. This fix was driven by the sample definition, not by any comparison with reported values. No Westfall-Young p-values computed (not requested). No run hung.
